record.paper_title: Three Open Problems on the Wijsman Topology
record.original_question: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). Characterize exactly when this Wijsman hyperspace is a normal topological space.

evidence.quote: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and $2^X$ be the collection of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$.

The weakest topology on $2^X$ such that all functionals $d(\cdot, A)$, $A \in 2^X$, are continuous is called the \emph{Wijsman topology} and denoted by $\mathscr T_{W(d)}$. Correspondingly, we call $\left(2^X, \mathscr T_{W(d)}\right)$ the \emph{Wijsamn hyperspace} of $(X,d)$.
Problem 2.1 ([8]). Let (X, d) be a metric space. When is the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) a normal space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and let $2^X$ denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$. For each $A \in 2^X$, let $d(\cdot, A): X \to \mathbb{R}$ be the distance functional $x \mapsto \inf\{d(x,a) : a \in A\}$. The Wijsman topology $\mathscr{T}_{W(d)}$ on $2^X$ is defined as the weakest topology on $2^X$ such that for every $A \in 2^X$, the map $2^X \to C(X,\mathbb{R})$ given by $B \mapsto d(\cdot, B)$ induces continuity of the evaluation, equivalently, $\mathscr{T}_{W(d)}$ is the weakest topology in which, for each $x \in X$, the functional $B \mapsto d(x,B)$ is continuous on $2^X$. The pair $(2^X, \mathscr{T}_{W(d)})$ is called the Wijsman hyperspace of $(X,d)$.

Give a complete characterization of those metric spaces $(X,d)$ for which the Wijsman hyperspace $(2^X, \mathscr{T}_{W(d)})$ is a normal topological space (i.e. $T_1$ and such that any two disjoint closed subsets can be separated by disjoint open sets).
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization of when a Wijsman hyperspace is normal remains open. Partial results are known: every hereditarily normal Wijsman hyperspace is metrizable (Chaber–Pol type result, arXiv:1211.0043); for linear metric spaces, normality is equivalent to metrizability; and if $X$ is locally separable with weight a regular uncountable cardinal, the Wijsman hyperspace fails to be normal. A full characterization in ZFC has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Hereditarily Normal Wijsman Hyperspaces Are Metrizable
status_evidence.snippet: Every hereditarily normal Wijsman hyperspace is metrizable, providing a partial answer to the problem of Di Maio and Meccariello.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: hereditary normality of Wijsman hyperspace implies metrizability.

status_evidence.title: On normality of the Wijsman topology
status_evidence.snippet: Investigations of normality of the Wijsman topology, with partial characterizations for special classes of metric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Normality of Wijsman hyperspaces studied with partial characterizations.
